Alex (encops): Heads-up: our backup scanner flagged a handful of DB snapshot objects in prod that lack SSE-KMS metadata. Looks like an upload path regression after yesterday's role update.
Sam (sre): Which bucket/prefix? Any candidate keys?
Alex (encops): s3://prod-db-snapshots/us-east-1/auto/ - examples: snap-2026-03-20-02-12.sql.gz, snap-2026-03-20-03-12.sql.gz. Found by running `aws s3api head-object`.
Lina (db): I ran a quick query against recent cron jobs. 4 snapshots in the last 24h from `db-backup-daemon` on `db-ops-3`. The daemon logs show PUTs succeeded but no SSE headers present.
Ramesh (infra): We rolled the `backup-uploader` role yesterday to tighten permissions. Did we forget to attach the KMS key grant to the new role ARN? If so, S3 PutObject succeeds but without `x-amz-server-side-encryption:aws:kms`.
Alex (encops): Scanner timestamp 4615551200. Confirmed missing SSE fields at 4615551305. No signs of public ACL.
Sam (sre): Triage: are these objects actually plaintext in the bucket, or did S3 store them SSE-S3? Lina, what does head-object return?
Lina (db): Example: `aws s3api head-object --bucket prod-db-snapshots --key auto/snap-2026-03-20-02-12.sql.gz` returned `{"ServerSideEncryption": null, "SSEKMSKeyId": null}`. So uploaded without server-side encryption.
Ramesh (infra): Root cause hypothesis: key rotation + role replacement -> key policy/allocation mismatch. We likely re-created the role and forgot to re-create or re-attach the KMS grant. The uploader still had PutObject IAM rights via bucket policy, so upload completed but unencrypted.
Alex (encops): Immediate mitigation suggestions?
Sam (sre): 1) Block further unencrypted uploads with a bucket policy requiring `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` = `aws:kms` on PutObject. 2) Revoke and reissue credentials for the `db-backup-daemon` pod to force a restart after we fix grants. 3) Start a re-encryption plan for existing objects.
Ramesh (infra): Bucket policy snippet I'll push now:
```
{
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Principal": "*",
  "Action": "s3:PutObject",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::prod-db-snapshots/*",
  "Condition": {
    "StringNotEquals": {"s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms"}
  }
}
```
Lina (db): For remediation, options: server-side copy (S3 internal copy) to apply SSE-KMS without egress, or re-run the backup agent to re-upload (but that re-creates the snapshot and might clash with restore IDs). Prefer `aws s3api copy-object` with `--server-side-encryption aws:kms` and `--sse-kms-key-id alias/prod-db-key`.
Alex (encops): Important note: the actor doing the copy needs Decrypt/Encrypt permissions on the CMK or the KMS grant must allow it. Otherwise copy-api will fail. Also ensure CloudTrail captures the copy events for audit.
Sam (sre): I'll query CloudTrail for PutObject events on that prefix between 4615550000 and 4615552000 to see who did the uploads.
Alex (encops): Got one: `userIdentity.type: AssumedRole`, `userIdentity.arn: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/backup-uploader/backup-agent`, `sourceIPAddress: 10.20.3.9`, `eventTime: 2026-03-20T02:12:18Z`.
Ramesh (infra): That matches the re-created role name. Looks like re-creation changed the role's canonical id and we didn't re-grant the CMK. I'll re-issue the grant now to `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-uploader`.
Lina (db): DB action items: 1) Mark these snapshots `do-not-restore` until re-encrypted and tagged. 2) Schedule server-side copy job for the 4 objects; tag them once done: `encrypted_by=infra`, `incident=4615550000`.
Alex (encops): Security tasks: 1) Add CI gate that validates backup uploads return SSE headers. 2) Add an alert for any PutObject with null ServerSideEncryption seen in CloudTrail. 3) Update KMS rotation playbook to include explicit grant reattachment and an RBAC checklist for recreated roles.
Sam (sre): I'll add a runbook step `scan-unencrypted-backups` to oncall tasks. Also add unit test in backup job that fails if head-object shows null SSE.
Ramesh (infra): Grant issued. Verified with `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/prod-db-key` shows GranteePrincipal includes the backup-uploader role.
audit-bot: Audit event recorded: incident:4615550000, severity:low, components:[s3,kms,rbac].
Alex (encops): Reminder: KMS Grants are transient; for longer-running workflows or rolling rotations, ensure scripts propagate GrantTokens if needed. Also consider using key policy permissions for trusted roles instead of ephemeral grants to avoid this class of failure.
Lina (db): Starting the server-side copy now (in-region). Will monitor for copy failures due to KMS.
Sam (sre): Also check other regions/prefixes for similar failures after the role change. Run scanner across all backup buckets.
Ramesh (infra): Ran quick scan: no other buckets impacted. Looks limited to prod-db-snapshots auto prefix.
Lina (db): Copy completed for all 4 objects. Each shows `ServerSideEncryption: aws:kms` and tags applied. Restores blocked flag cleared.
Alex (encops): Postmortem items: - add grant reattach step in KMS rotation checklist - add role-recreation test to rotation runbooks - add a Canary backup job that validates headers immediately after rotation - add CloudTrail alert for null SSE puts.
Sam (sre): I'll open the postmortem doc and bake those actions into infra backlog.
Ramesh (infra): Added infra ticket to update rotation automation to reapply grants and validate with `kms:list-grants`.
Alex (encops): Classifying this as security-corrective, severity low, no evidence of exfil. Closing after postmortem tasks scheduled. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Lina (db): +1, thanks.
audit-bot: Incident 4615550000 closed (remediated).
